rows.claim: An input trace replays any run bit-identically
rows.evidence: design/spec.md:664-667 and 6303-6307 qualify the promise: it holds only against the identical build running identical compiled code. A trace recorded at one optimization level does not replay bit for bit at another. src/sim.jl:1334 replay! checks the checkpoint fingerprint, so a different deployment is refused.
rows.note: The introduction states the promise without the condition that the body of the spec (§2.4, §9.7) attaches to it. This is an inconsistency inside the spec, not a code divergence.
rows.fix: An input trace that replays a run bit-identically on the same build and compiled code ([§11.5][s11-5]).

ok.claim: A hybrid causal system has five parts, as the five bullets list
f also receives the signal table (x, u, y, t in the RHS entry)
Discrete components update at declared rates and hold outputs between ticks
A tick is an instant at which a discrete component's stages and update run
State events run under two detection policies, localized and non-localized
The projection hook is x_projection(c, x), optional per component
Projection is applied at every boundary, boundary zero included
Projection is applied after any handler reset of x
Root inputs change only at frame tops and hold between writes
Frame tops are t0 + k*Δt_frame, Δt_frame is a Deployment keyword
Frame tops and base ticks are two lattices in no required ratio
Every discrete schedule falls on the base-tick lattice
Each instant is computed from its own index, never accumulated
The origin is held exact and each clock is the float nearest its instant
A time typed on a lattice equals its boundary's clock
Coincidence is decided on the exact periods (integer units), not on computed times
The lattices are fixed for the run, and a located event never moves a later instant
Mandatory instants are the frame tops and the due instants
No integration step crosses a mandatory instant
A base tick at which no component is due is not a mandatory instant
A boundary is an instant where discrete changes happen and the run publishes
Every frame top after t0 is a boundary
Every integration step end inside a frame is a boundary
Every localized event time t* is a boundary
The origin is a boundary once (boundary zero), with no integration before it
Frame 1's top follows boundary zero at the same instant
A base tick with nothing due is no boundary
Every due instant is a boundary and a due instant inside a frame ends its step
Step ends inside a frame and t* are boundaries but not frame tops
Fixed-step interior end is the span start plus its count times the exact step
Adaptive interior end is the step's start plus its length
Diagram: t0 boundary zero, d due instant, s step end, t* localized, t1 and t2 frame tops
Distinct boundaries other than t* take strictly increasing clocks
A run whose clock cannot order two boundaries is refused (ArgumentInvalid :range)
The refusal does not cover t*
Discrete components tick only at boundaries
Modes change during a run only through handlers, which run only at boundaries
Root inputs change only at frame tops
Time is held in no store, and a condition cannot set it (set takes x, s, m, u only)
The origin is fixed at init! and unchanged after boundary zero
The origin anchors both lattices and every discrete tick schedule
A restored run keeps the clock and the origin of the restored state
The integration method is chosen at the deployment (algorithm keyword)
A fixed-step method takes a span in the fewest equal steps of at most h_max
A span of length l takes N = ceil(l/h_max) steps of l/N
With no h_max a span takes one step
The bound need divide neither period
Steps of a span are equal unless a localized event splits one
The split into steps follows the schedule, not the state
A due instant ends a step whether or not anything discrete changes
A model at dual numbers freezes its discrete tier
A Dual model takes the same steps as the Float64 model
An adaptive method proposes each step's length from its error estimate
The run takes the distance to the next mandatory instant in the fewest equal steps within the proposal and h_max
The floor h_min wins over the proposed length
No step is shorter than the floor unless less than the floor remains
A rejected step is retried shorter and a step at the floor is accepted
A step integrates by the distance between its clocks, or by its proposed length
A localized event with no crossing leaves the step as it would be without the event
Each step starts from the state the last boundary left, after resets and projection
One-step methods carry no solution history
An adaptive method's controller keeps a memory of past steps
The run notifies the method of every jump: handler reset, tick or drain write
Inside a step discrete outputs hold the values of their last tick
Before its first tick a discrete component's outputs hold boundary-zero values
Root inputs are the only channel from outside into a running model
Nothing outside the model writes its state, modes or outputs during a run
Root inputs change only at frame tops
Writers stage values at any wall-clock moment
The drain applies staged writes before the frame integrates
A root input never changes inside a frame
A root input keeps its last applied value until a writer sets it again
When several values are staged for one root input, the newest takes effect
The boundary ending a frame completes and publishes before the next frame's drain
A tick at a frame top samples the root-input values the ending frame held
A tick at a due instant inside a frame samples the values that frame holds
A staged value first reaches the model in the frame that its drain opens
Pause, pace and stop do not change what a step computes
